resources.string: What Safeer needs and why – switch on with one tap

Safeer only asks for what it really uses. The button opens the right settings page – switch Safeer on there and come back. For “display over other apps” Android shows a list of apps: find Safeer in it. You can revoke anything at any time.
Something important is still missing, so Safeer Link can\'t do everything on this device. Tap “Allow” on the marked rows.
So Safeer Link can open an app or page you send from your computer or phone on this device.
Requests and messages from other devices in Link (e.g. “Allow this device internet?”) and confirmations.
So a confirmation request (new device, deleting a photo) appears over the screen, even when the device is locked.
So you see them in Files and Media Center and can share them with other devices in Link.
So Media Center can play music from this device and share it with other devices.
So your computer\'s mouse and keyboard can control this device through Safeer Link (accessibility).
So Safeer can install its new versions (Android still asks you before each install).
Is the switch grey or won\'t it move?
1. On the system page, tap Safeer\'s grey switch once – Android says the setting is restricted. Close that message.
2. Tap the button below, then ⋮ at the top right and choose “Allow restricted settings” (on Samsung it may be right on the page). Come back here and tap “Allow” again.
Android requires this for apps installed outside a store. Safeer cannot switch it on by itself.
A paired device wanted to open %1$s. Tap “Allow”, then “Allow” next to “%2$s”. Android shows a list of apps: find “%3$s” and switch it on. Then send the command again. Once is enough.
On this device, allow “%1$s” for Safeer once (the notification is already on screen, or Safeer › Settings › Permissions), then start %2$s again.
A paired device wanted to open %1$s. Tap “Allow”: Android opens “%2$s” with a list of apps – find “%3$s”, switch it on and send the command again. Once is enough.
